clusters.title: Two universal claims on this page are refuted by its own tables: 2.5 'julieta never guesses paths' beside six $HOME-derived paths (julieta symlink, secondaries, state, hook dispatcher, mise, herdr) no manifest field carries, and 2.4 'ROMEU_SETTINGS is the only environment override' beside XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME locating settings and state.
clusters.scenario: A contributor trusts 'never guesses paths' and adds a $HOME path outside the manifest; the workload user changes from agent and the manifest path romeu wrote (03 3.6) disagrees with $HOME; a herdr release moves its config dir and the 06 6.4 settings stop applying unnoticed; a test sets XDG_STATE_HOME and the sentence says nothing happens.
clusters.change: 02 2.5: replace the closing sentence with 'julieta takes repo, memory, spool, view and binary paths from the manifest (03 3.6) or its own executable path; the rows owned by julieta or the julieta mixin derive from $HOME by rule, and the mise and herdr rows are those tools' upstream defaults at the pinned versions, which the julieta mixin sets explicitly through the environment (MISE_DATA_DIR, the herdr config path) so a moved default changes nothing.' 03 3.6: name the source of the sandbox home romeu writes into the manifest (the workload's recorded user home, measured by probe A4 and stored with the pin). 02 2.4: write 'ROMEU_SETTINGS is the only romeu-specific environment variable; XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME are honoured as shown; the root comes only from the settings file.' 02 2.6: date the 'documented sbx behavior' (sbx version and doc date) and name A3 as the probe that re-confirms it. The 10 10.6 and 04 4.1 halves of L3-21 are resolved on those pages.
clusters.cost: Four sentences; one measured fact recorded by A4.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed: reword the 2.5 and 2.4 claims to what is true, have the mixin set the mise and herdr paths explicitly, name the sandbox-home source in 03 3.6, date the 2.6 sbx behavior and tie it to A3.

clusters.title: The tree has one cmd/<binary>/main.go and one internal/cli dispatcher for about 36 commands built by about 25 tasks, so every command PR edits the same shared files and tools/new command writes into a file the spec never names.
clusters.scenario: Phase 4 builds sync, approve, status, doctor and adopt concurrently; each PR edits cmd/romeu/main.go and the dispatcher's list and conflicts with the next merge.
clusters.change: 02 2.1: add 'internal/cmd/romeu/<command>/ and internal/cmd/julieta/<command>/   one package per command; the dispatcher table in internal/cli is generated from them (12 12.3, command definitions)'. 12 12.3: one sentence that tools/new command creates the command's package and reference entry and edits no shared file; the existing command-definitions generator emits the table.
clusters.cost: Two tree lines, one sentence; reuses the command-definitions generator.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form: no new generator, the existing 12 12.3 command-definitions row emits the dispatcher table; two tree lines and one sentence in 12 12.3.

clusters.title: Embedding says the julieta binaries are embedded 'at release time' but not what a plain source build (go build, go install @vX) embeds or whether it refuses to run.
clusters.scenario: A GPL user builds romeu from the tag; it fails to compile for a missing go:embed file, or embeds a julieta the release never produced, which render.json then trusts as delivered (I30).
clusters.change: 02 2.1, after Embedding: 'A source build without tools/release build embeds a placeholder; romeu built that way refuses run, sync and promotion with exit 2 and error id julieta-not-embedded, and every other command works. tools/release build is the only supported way to embed julieta; contributor e2e builds go through it (10 10.2).' Add the error id to the 04 error table.
clusters.cost: A paragraph and one error id.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply with the placeholder-plus-refusal form only; no second build path.

clusters.title: The config repo's validate.yml runs a downloaded julieta release that nothing verifies by bytes; julieta pin check --workflows checks freshness only.
clusters.scenario: A replaced release asset runs in the operator's config-repo CI with no checksum or attestation check.
clusters.change: 02 2.2: change the validate.yml line to 'runs julieta spec validate --catalog projects/*.yaml from a julieta release pinned by version and archive sha256, verified against the release's checksums.txt before it runs (checked by julieta pin check)'. 04 4.3: pin check --workflows compares the pinned sha256 with checksums.txt. examples/ ships that validate.yml.
clusters.cost: One pin format, one check, one example workflow.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply with a sha256 pin and the checksums.txt comparison; the attestation check follows whatever 10 10.2 decides for release attestation, not a second contract here.

clusters.title: Salvage refs live only in host clones the spec calls plain operator clones, and the owner is told neither that deleting or re-cloning one loses them nor that git push --mirror publishes them (salvage commits can hold untracked files).
clusters.scenario: The operator re-clones a secondary's navigation clone (2.6) or follows J13 step 4; three generations of salvage refs go and status keeps reporting the salvage complete. Or, after leaving the product, a mirror push publishes refs/romeu/salvage/* with dirty files, possibly secrets.
clusters.change: 02 2.3, after the ref namespaces: 'These refs belong to the clone they are in: deleting or re-cloning it loses them, and git push --mirror publishes them. List them with git for-each-ref refs/romeu refs/sandboxes.' 02 2.6: drop 'plain' from 'a plain operator clone' and point to that sentence. doctor (04 4.2) fails, with a new error id naming the record, when a ref under a salvage record's refsPrefix is missing from its clone. J13 step 4: 'after status shows nothing unpushed and no salvage-only refs'. J14 gains the for-each-ref step for removal once nothing in them is needed.
clusters.cost: Three sentences, one doctor row, one error id, two guide steps.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as one owner-facing statement in 2.3 plus the one doctor check; no new storage for salvage refs.

clusters.title: 'every state transition of a project is a single atomic write' is false for promotion, salvage and retire, and retire makes two moves (tree under $ROMEU_ROOT, record under $XDG_STATE_HOME) with no recovery rule.
clusters.scenario: retire moves <name>-env to .attic and is killed before moving the record; the next sync finds a live record with no tree and recreates <name>-env with empty memory dirs beside the attic copy.
clusters.change: 02 2.4: replace the sentence with 'Each record write is atomic; a transition that changes more than one file follows its step list in 01 1.6.' 01 1.6: add the retire step list: write state retiring to the record, move the tree to .attic, move the record to attic/; any command that finds a record in retiring finishes the remaining steps before anything else, and sync never recreates a tree for a retiring record.
clusters.cost: A sentence and a three-step list.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed.

clusters.title: No mode is fixed for the host tree that holds memory, salvage payloads, spool, view, .attic and review checkouts; only settings, state and the ledger have one and doctor checks only those.
clusters.scenario: On a Mac with a second local account, memory entries, handoffs and salvage payloads under $HOME/dev are world-readable under the default umask.

Add the case to I24. Probe A3 records that the direct mounts keep the modes as the sandbox sees them.

clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form: fix the mode on the two parent directories (<name>-env/, .attic/) rather than on each subdirectory, so one doctor row covers the tree.

clusters.title: 02 2.1's package tree and its '(romeu only)', '(julieta only)' and '(shared)' comments are a hand copy of 10 10.7's boundary table and 12 12.2's module map, with different names for the same code, and 10 10.7 is fail-open for a package no row names.

clusters.title: Memory dirs and the spool are agent-writable host directories under $HOME/dev that host indexers (Spotlight importers, Quick Look, Time Machine) parse without the operator opening anything, while 05 5.4 speaks only of an operator who opens the directory and boundary D's 'no host tool is pointed at an agent-writable tree' is false for them.

clusters.change: 02 2.3: sync creates <name>-env/.metadata_never_index (outside every mount, so I24 is untouched) and the tree shows it with 'keeps Spotlight from parsing agent-written files'. 04 4.2: doctor warns when the marker is missing or $ROMEU_ROOT is inside a Time Machine-included or cloud-synced path. 05 5.4: widen the residual-risk row to host indexers. 01 1.3 boundary D: name what is checked.
clusters.cost: One file written by sync, one doctor row, two sentences, one 5.4 row change.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend applying: the marker and the doctor warning are cheap and inside the spec; the 05 5.4 row widening is the operator's call.
clusters.operator_reason: Widens an accepted residual-risk row in 05 5.4.

clusters.title: 'secondary repos need the project's git credential inside the sandbox' and 07 7.4's 'the github secret covers it' rest on a mechanism the spec never states (how a named secret becomes the credential git, gh and mise present to GitHub in the sandbox) and that no probe measures; 10 10.3 lists credential injection under Cannot model.
clusters.scenario: The operator binds github@shop; the agent's push fails or succeeds for reasons the spec cannot name; B3 after the candidate tag is the first to see it.

Add to probe A3 (not a new probe) a check that a sandbox with a scoped github secret can clone a private secondary, push a branch and call the GitHub API.

clusters.resolution_text: Apply with the check folded into A3 rather than a new probe.

clusters.title: projects/<name>.json holds generations[] (each with salvage[]) appended forever in a file rewritten whole on every mutating command, with no bound and no compaction.
clusters.scenario: Years of recreate give several hundred generations; every run rewrites the record and status parses it on every call; S8 is measured against an empty record.
clusters.change: 03 3.8: 'The record keeps every generation in v1; it grows by one generation per recreate and has no bound.' Add a Deferred decisions row 'compact closed generations into the state attic', trigger 'the first record over 256 KiB, or status measured slower than S8 on a real record'; doctor warns past 256 KiB.
clusters.cost: One sentence, one deferred row, one doctor row.
clusters.resolution_text: State the growth as a limit and defer compaction with a measured trigger; no move-on-close mechanism in v1.

clusters.title: The spec never says where the user edits and debugs day to day: dev.code-workspace is rewritten on every promotion, carries I13 and I14, is opened by no journey and only in Restricted Mode, while romeu pull, the review checkout and review.code-workspace serve a host review path the start does not need (ADR 0008 makes the PR the review barrier).

Either delete dev.code-workspace or give it a J-step; in either case add to 02 2.3 one sentence naming the supported daily setup in v1: editing and debugging happen inside the sandbox (the agent's panes, or VS Code attached to the sandbox when Remote-SSH arrives in v1.1), and host clones are for reading in Restricted Mode only.
clusters.cost: Deletions in 01, 02, 04, 05, 09; the plan loses most of T067; one sentence in 2.3.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend deferring pull and review.code-workspace and deleting dev.code-workspace, plus the one-sentence daily-setup statement in 2.3 (which can be applied on its own now).
clusters.operator_reason: Removes a v1 command from scope (00 0.3) and two accepted residual-risk rows from 05 5.4.
